title: Emergency superuser override protocol (SSO/SAML, RBAC v2, audit)
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Problem: We currently lack a formally documented and instrumented emergency admin flow that integrates with RBAC v2, SSO/SAML identity providers, and immutable audit logging. On-call engineers have resorted to ad-hoc token sharing and manual IAM changes during incidents. This ticket defines a repeatable, auditable superuser-override protocol for P0/P1 incidents that balances fast mitigation with compliance and traceability.

Scope: design and implement a short-lived emergency access mechanism that: 1) requires multi-factor approval when possible (on-call + security lead), 2) issues time-limited superuser sessions tied to SSO identity (no static keys), 3) records session activity into our audit logging pipeline (append-only, tamper-evident), and 4) automatically revokes privileges and triggers post-incident workflow (rotation, postmortem link). Integrations: RBAC v2 role elevations, SSO/SAML provider (Okta), audit logging (Stackdriver -> ELK pipeline), and Console UI for approvals and session status.

Out-of-scope: building a full-fledged ticketing approval UI (we'll link to PagerDuty/GitHub approvals for initial rollout), long-term cryptographic HSM storage for emergency keys (covered in a follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: Design doc with sequence diagrams and threat model reviewed by Security and Infra
Implementation: emergency session issuance using SSO assertion with max TTL 15 minutes
Approval flow requires two approvers (on-call + security or engineering lead) for production superuser elevation
All elevated sessions emit structured audit events (JSON) to audit pipeline within 30s of action
Automatic revocation: session tokens revoked after TTL or on manual termination; revocation visible in Console and in audit logs
Post-incident hook: creating an incident review checklist link and required rotation tasks created automatically after any manual override
workplan: Draft design + threat model (Asha) - include RBAC v2 role mapping and SSO assertion flow
Prototype server-side endpoint to mint short-lived emergency sessions (Diego) - integrate with SSO provider for claims
Wire Console approval panel and status indicators (frontend) - show active emergency sessions and allow kill/revoke
Hook audit logging: ensure structured event schema and immutable append (Infra) - add pipeline validation tests
Run tabletop drills with oncall and security for three scenarios (data exfil, control plane outage, customer incident)
Security review and signoff; ship behind feature flag for initial region (us-west-2)
notes: Design constraint: emergency access must not create persistent service credentials. All sessions must be tied to an SSO identity assertion and generate an auditable principal ID.
We will reuse RBAC v2 temporary elevation APIs where possible; if gaps exist, create minimal extension endpoints rather than broad changes.
Audit events must include: actor_saml_id, approvers, reason, TTL, issued_at, revoked_at, session_id, actions_summary (list of top-level actions).
Plan for future: add session recording (terminal/console) and integrate with forensics team for post-incident playback.
